guarantees.claim: status_o is combinatorially assigned: OpDoneFail when op_done_o && (error_o || fault_o); OpDoneSuccess when op_done_o && !(error_o || fault_o); OpWip else if op_start_i; OpIdle otherwise.

assumptions.claim: When op_done_o is high, error_o and fault_o must be valid Boolean values (no X/Z).
assumptions.risk: If undefined, status_o becomes X, potentially propagating to downstream safety/error logic.

assumptions.claim: op_start_i must be externally gated by the enable signal (en_i) such that it only asserts when the interface is truly active.
assumptions.risk: If op_start_i asserts spuriously (when en_i low), status_o will show OpWip, fooling downstream logic into thinking an operation is in progress.

uncertain_points.claim: The comment describes a one‑cycle‑behind main FSM and an enable signal (en_i) not present in this block; it is unclear whether status_o aligns correctly with the enabled FSM state when en_i goes low the same cycle op_done_o asserts.
uncertain_points.cond: op_done_o asserts in the cycle en_i goes low
uncertain_points.risk: The consumer may interpret a done/fail status while the interface is disabled, leading to incorrect state transitions or missed operations.
